title: Avoid Dynamic Code Execution
content: Do not invoke eval(), exec(), or compile() on dynamic strings or untrusted parameters. These permit arbitrary remote code execution (RCE). Parse input with strict typing or AST literal evaluators.

title: Avoid Bare Exception Handling
content: Do not use unadorned except blocks ('except:'). They trap critical process interrupts such as SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt, concealing fatal defects and blocking graceful container restarts. Target specific exceptions.

title: Prevent Hardcoded Secrets and Tokens
content: API keys, database credentials, and secret signing keys must never be hardcoded in application logic. Store them in secret managers or inject them via environment variables at deployment.

title: SQL Injection Safeguards
content: Never concatenate raw user strings into SQL queries. Always utilize parameterized queries, bind variables, or an Object Relational Mapper (ORM) like SQLAlchemy or Tortoise.

title: Asynchronous Non-Blocking Handlers
content: In high-concurrency event loops (like FastAPI), never execute synchronous blocking network calls (e.g. requests.get or time.sleep). Use httpx.AsyncClient and asyncio.sleep to prevent event-loop starvation.

title: Cache Invalidation & In-Memory Storage
content: When caching database lookups in Redis or Memcached, define explicit Time-To-Live (TTL) horizons and adopt write-through or cache-aside strategies to prevent reading stale, corrupted state.

title: Layered Separation of Responsibilities
content: Decouple HTTP routing layers from business domain services and data persistence layers. API routers should validate request schemas and delegate business logic to decoupled services.

title: Connection Pooling for Database Connections
content: Creating a new database TCP handshake on every HTTP request produces excessive connection overhead. Maintain a persistent asynchronous connection pool with configured max_overflow limits.

title: Idempotent Queue Consumer Design
content: Distributed message queues (Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS) provide at-least-once delivery guarantees. Consumers must maintain idempotency via unique deduplication keys or transactional checkpoints.

title: External Service Timeouts and Circuit Breakers
content: Calls to third-party APIs or remote microservices must define aggressive timeouts and circuit breaker patterns to prevent cascaded failures and thread pool saturation during downstream outages.
